prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a side impact at intersection claim. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1314; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened for a side impact collision at a controlled intersection. Insured vehicle was struck on the driver side by a second vehicle that entered the intersection against a red signal, per the initial statement from the insured. Police report requested. Tow arranged for the insured vehicle.

Entry 2: Spoke with the claimant by phone. Claimant reports a wrist fracture sustained in the impact and is currently being treated at an urgent care clinic. Claimant is not represented by an attorney. Explained the claims process and the documentation needed for the injury portion of the claim. Requested medical records and the treatment plan.

Entry 3: Received the responding officer's report. It notes both drivers gave consistent accounts of the signal phase, and one witness at the corner confirmed the other vehicle ran the red light. Contact information for the witness has been added to the file. Liability appears clear on the available evidence.

Entry 4: Claimant provided photos of the vehicle damage and a copy of the initial X-ray report showing a fracture of the wrist. Follow-up orthopedic appointment is scheduled. Reviewed the coverage limits under the policy and confirmed that medical payments coverage applies to the claimant as an occupant of the insured vehicle, pending verification of the claimant's role at the time of loss.

Entry 5: Sent the claimant a written summary of the injury claim process, including how to submit ongoing medical bills and wage loss documentation. Claimant was advised that they may wish to seek independent advice before accepting any settlement offer. Diary set to follow up after the orthopedic consultation.
